title: site-config/1 — the config a protocol repository's institutional front door is generated from
description: One document per property, validated as site-config/1. build-site.mjs reads it, plus the repository's own .well-known/stack.json copy, its AAO charter and the vendored brand kit, and writes the whole site/. Everything property-specific lives here, so the generator itself is vendored unchanged across the estate's protocol repositories. Keys prefixed x- are extensions and allowed anywhere; every other key is closed.

property.description: The property slug, e.g. web4. Machine-safe.

domain.description: The property's own domain, or null when it has none yet and deploys at the estate Pages URL. Never a guess.

layer.description: How this property sits in the stack — a stack layer name, or 'the map' for the hub.

contract.description: The protocol contract this property carries, e.g. web4/1 or intent/1 — a lower-case slug, a slash, a dotted version.

accent.description: The one brand accent, named as a --flashy-* token from the vendored brand/tokens.css. The generator resolves it to a hex; a name that names no token fails the build.

refusals.description: The property's structural refusals — what a caller cannot do, phrased as a refusal, one per principle.

faq.description: Questions a stranger asks, answered in a couple of honest sentences each. Rendered with FAQPage JSON-LD.

links.description: The three links the front door always carries: the human hub, the machine twin or spec, and this repository.
